message.content:
Repo location: H:\Kasirku (a Next.js + Supabase multi-tenant POS/accounting SaaS called "Kasirku", live at createimpact.id, GitHub melansamudra/Kasirku).

Context: the owner wants to onboard a new F&B (restaurant/culinary) client onto this platform. The client asked for cashier features "similar to Moka POS" specifically: printer settings, receipt/struk printing, and shift open/close reports with cash reconciliation. We already confirmed (via browsing GitHub) that Kasirku has an open_shift/close_shift RPC (supabase/migrations/20260702100900_shift_rpc.sql), a checkout_transaction RPC, an open-shift-screen.tsx and pos-screen.tsx under src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/, printer management under src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/settings/ (add-printer-form.tsx, delete-printer-button.tsx), and a shifts history page under (dashboard)/shifts. There's also an F&B-specific migration 20260702100200_products_ingredients_recipes.sql and 20260702100500_fnb_support_tables.sql, plus a "tables" folder and self-order-via-QR feature (order/[qrSlug]).

Your job: thoroughly read the actual code (not just skim) to build a concrete feature inventory relevant to a typical F&B cashier's daily workflow, so we can compare it against Moka POS and identify real gaps. Specifically report on, with file paths and line numbers where relevant:

1. **Shift lifecycle**: How does open_shift/close_shift actually work end-to-end in the UI (src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/open-shift-screen.tsx, pos-screen.tsx)? Does it support cash-in/cash-out mid-shift (kas masuk/keluar)? Is there a printable/viewable shift report after closing? Check (dashboard)/shifts/ folder contents.
2. **Printer settings**: What can be configured in settings/add-printer-form.tsx — LAN printer (IP/port) like ESC/POS, Bluetooth, or USB/browser print only? Is printer selection exposed to the cashier during a shift, or only in back-office settings? Is there a kitchen/bar ticket printing concept (multi-station printing) like a KDS, or just one receipt printer?
3. **Receipt/struk**: Where do receipts get printed from (transactions/ folder, "Auto-open print dialog on receipt pages")? Can a cashier reprint a past receipt from within the POS session (not just back-office)? What does the receipt template look like (store name, tax, footer, paper size 58mm/80mm)?
4. **F&B specifics**: Does the menu/product model support variants (e.g. size Regular/Jumbo) and print-station routing per category (kitchen vs bar) like a typical restaurant POS? Check products_ingredients_recipes.sql and fnb_support_tables.sql, and the "tables" (dine-in table) feature.
5. **Cashier PIN / multi-cashier**: How does pin-screen.tsx / switch-cashier-button.tsx work — can multiple cashiers use the same shift, or one shift per cashier?

Report back a structured summary organized by these 5 topics, each with: what exists (concrete, with file:line references), and what's clearly MISSING or weaker compared to a full-featured F&B POS like Moka POS (be specific, not generic). Keep total report under 900 words. Do not write or edit any files — this is read-only research.

No `@media print` width rules elsewhere — confirms receipt is just a fixed `max-w-xs` (browser print, relies on OS print dialog paper size selection), not an explicit 58mm/80mm toggle.

## Feature Inventory: Kasirku vs. Moka POS-style Cashier Workflow

**Repo: `H:\Kasirku`**

### 1. Shift lifecycle
End-to-end flow: `pos/page.tsx:51-67` checks for an open shift for the **business** (not per-cashier) via `shifts` table where `closed_at is null`. No shift → `OpenShiftScreen` (`open-shift-screen.tsx`) posts `opening_cash`+notes to `open_shift` RPC (`20260702100900_shift_rpc.sql:5-49`), which blocks a second concurrent shift per business (line 30-35). Closing happens inline inside `pos-screen.tsx:672-733` (`closingShift` view) → `closeShift` action → `close_shift` RPC (lines 53-135) which tallies `transaction_payments` by method, computes `expected_cash = opening_cash + cash_sales`, `difference`, `tx_count`, `void_count`, and returns a summary shown in a "Shift Ditutup" screen (`pos-screen.tsx:617-670`). History at `(dashboard)/shifts/page.tsx` lists last 50 closed shifts with the same reconciliation fields but is **back-office only** (no print button, no per-transaction breakdown, no export).

**Missing vs. Moka**: No mid-shift cash-in/cash-out ("kas masuk/keluar" from the till, e.g. paying a supplier or topping up change). The only cash-in/out feature is `kas-harian` (`(dashboard)/kas-harian/actions.ts:9-60`), a general accounting journal entry (posts to `post_journal_entry` RPC) that is **not linked to `shift_id`** and not reflected in `close_shift`'s `expected_cash` math — so any till cash movements during a shift are invisible to the reconciliation. No printable end-of-shift "Z-report"; the close-shift summary is only an on-screen modal (no print button) and the shifts history page also has no print/reprint action. One shift is shared business-wide across cashiers (see §5), so there's no per-cashier shift accountability if two cashiers work simultaneously.

### 2. Printer settings
`add-printer-form.tsx` (`settings/add-printer-form.tsx:1-113`) lets the owner add a "Kitchen Printer" (`kitchen_printers` table, `20260702100500_fnb_support_tables.sql:21-28`) with a name, connection type toggle (Bluetooth vs LAN/Wi-Fi, lines 44-68), an address field (IP for LAN, device name for Bluetooth, line 70-81), and per-category routing checkboxes (lines 83-100) — this is genuine multi-station/KDS-style routing. Actual dispatch (`src/lib/kitchen-print.ts:43-87`) only implements **LAN** printers: opens a raw TCP socket to `host:port` (default port 9100, line 16) and writes ESC/POS bytes built by `src/lib/escpos.ts` (32-column-ish thermal ticket with station header, bold item lines, notes, partial cut). **Bluetooth entries are stored but never actually printed to** — `dispatchKitchenPrint` filters `connection_type === "lan"` only (`kitchen-print.ts:55-57`), so a Bluetooth printer configured in settings is silently a no-op. Printing triggers from `pos/actions.ts:129-136` (on `checkout`) and `pos/actions.ts:353-383` (on marking a self-order "diproses") — this is real kitchen-ticket routing by product category, filtered per printer's assigned categories (`kitchen-print.ts:59-67`). Printer config is **settings/back-office only**; there is no printer picker or manual "reprint to kitchen" control in `pos-screen.tsx` for the cashier.

**Missing vs. Moka**: no actual Bluetooth transport (stored config is dead), no USB printer support, no printer status/health check, no way for the cashier to manually resend/reprint a kitchen ticket from the POS screen, no receipt (customer copy) auto-print — only kitchen tickets are auto-dispatched; the customer receipt still requires a manual browser print (see §3).

### 3. Receipt/struk
Receipt lives at `(dashboard)/transactions/[transactionId]/receipt/page.tsx` — shows store name, invoice number, date, cashier name, itemized lines, subtotal/item-disc/order-disc/service/tax/total, payment method + received/change, and a "Terima kasih!" footer (lines 60-161). `print-button.tsx` auto-fires `window.print()` on mount (lines 17-22) — plain CSS `print:` Tailwind classes, `max-w-xs` (fixed width, no explicit 58mm/80mm CSS toggle — relies on the OS print dialog's paper size). From the till, `pos-screen.tsx:592-599` shows a "🖨️ Cetak Struk" link to this same page right after a successful checkout, opened in a new tab.

**Missing vs. Moka**: the cashier **cannot reprint a past receipt from within the POS session** — the only path back to `/transactions/[id]/receipt` for older sales is through the back-office `(dashboard)/transactions` list (`transactions/page.tsx`), which sits behind owner-account auth (`(dashboard)` layout), not the cashier PIN session. No paper-width setting (58mm/80mm) anywhere in code/CSS — purely relies on generic browser print. No direct-to-ESC/POS receipt printing (only kitchen tickets use `escpos.ts`); the customer receipt path is 100% "open a page, browser print dialog."

### 4. F&B specifics
Products support **variants** as separate rows sharing a name, grouped client-side by `name` in `pos-screen.tsx:188-201`, distinguished by `sku`/`variant_label` columns added in `20260712140000_product_sku_variants.sql:6-8` (comment there: "variants are just extra product rows... no schema relationship"). Print-station routing per **category** (not per-product) exists via `kitchen_printers.categories` as described in §2. `tables` (`20260702100500_fnb_support_tables.sql:41-55`) has `qr_slug` for QR-based self-order (`src/app/order/[qrSlug]`), feeding into `self_orders`/`self_order_items` (lines 66-115), which surface in POS as an "Order Masuk" inbox (`pos-screen.tsx:1419-1533`) with per-order Proses/Selesai status and auto kitchen-print on "diproses". Recipes/ingredients (`20260702100200_products_ingredients_recipes.sql`) support HPP costing via `product_recipes` linking products to `ingredients` with qty/unit, consumed via a separate recipe-consumption migration.

**Missing vs. Moka**: variants are unstructured (no real "attribute" model — e.g., no shared parent product with size/price matrix UI; just naming convention), no true dine-in table-status board (open/occupied/needs-bill) beyond the self-order QR flow — `tables/page.tsx` is closer to a QR-link manager than a floor-plan view. No course/timing control (fire now vs. hold) typical of full KDS. No modifier/add-on system distinct from full separate SKUs.

### 5. Cashier PIN / multi-cashier
`pin-screen.tsx` shows active cashiers (from `cashiers` table) and a 4-digit PIN pad; `verifyPin` (`pos/actions.ts:16-47`) calls `verify_cashier_pin` RPC and sets a session cookie (`setCashierSession`). `switch-cashier-button.tsx` simply clears the session cookie (`clearCashierSession`), forcing re-auth via `pin-screen.tsx` — available both before starting a shift (`open-shift-screen.tsx:106`) and mid-shift (`pos-screen.tsx:1249`).

**Missing vs. Moka**: since shifts are scoped to the **business**, not the **cashier** (`open_shift` RPC blocks any second open shift per business, `shift_rpc.sql:30-35`), multiple cashiers effectively **share one open shift** — switching cashier changes who is attributed on new transactions but does not create a separate shift/drawer per person, so there's no per-cashier drawer accountability or independent open/close within the same business at the same time (e.g., two registers running in parallel isn't supported — one shift per business at a time).
